Fix error when setting animation loop count (#2904)

When creating an animation with a custom loop count, via, e.g., `gif(anim; loop=-1)`, so `mov(anim; loop=-1)`, FFMPEG throws the following error:

```
[image2 demuxer @ 000001fdf77ec280] Unable to parse option value "-1" as boolean
[image2 demuxer @ 000001fdf77ec280] Error setting option loop to value -1. 
```

This PR fixes the error by moving the `-loop` flag to after the `-i` input flag in the call to `ffmpeg_exe`. I believe the error is caused because the `-loop` flag occuring before `-i` controls how the input is interpreted, whereas the `-loop` flag occuring after `-i` controls how many loops are in the output.

fix `aspect_ratio` corrupting 3D axis limits (#5775)

`axis_limits` passed the symbol `:sp` to `RecipesPipeline.is3d`, which resolves
to the `is3d(st) = false` fallback, so the guard never fired for 3D. The 2D
aspect correction then widened x/y limits on 3D subplots by a factor derived
from the plot area's pixel dimensions.

Fixes #3419.

Plots: fix `atreplinit` hook registration (#5780)

The REPL-init hook that moves PlotsDisplay above the REPL display was
written as `i -> begin ... end |> atreplinit`, which parses as
`i -> (begin ... end |> atreplinit)` because `|>` binds tighter than
`->`: the whole statement builds an anonymous function that is never
called, so the hook was never registered. As a result, when Plots is
loaded before the REPL starts (for example from `startup.jl` or via
`julia -i -e "using Plots"`), PlotsDisplay stays below the REPL display
in `Base.Multimedia.displays` and plots only show their text summary
instead of reaching the GUI display. Pass the closure to `atreplinit`
directly.

set `scene.aspectmode` for 3D `plotly` subplots (#5777)

The 3D scene never set `aspectmode`, leaving plotly.js on its `"auto"` default:
box proportional to the data, except past a 4x span ratio where it falls back
to `"cube"`. That made `plotly` the only backend whose 3D proportions depend on
the data, since `GR` (`setwindow3d`) and `PythonPlot` (`set_box_aspect`) always
cube. Default to `"cube"` so the box no longer varies with the data.

`aspect_ratio = :equal` now maps to `"manual"` with the ratio taken from the
axis limits, which makes one data unit the same length on every axis. `"data"`
cannot express this: despite its documentation plotly derives it from the extent
of the traces and ignores `xlims`/`ylims`/`zlims`, so an explicitly limited
subplot got a box that did not match its own axes.

Also skip `plotly_apply_aspect_ratio` for 3D, where it shrinks the scene domain
by an x/y data ratio that means nothing under a 3D projection, and threw on
vector `aspect_ratio`.

Backport of the `v2` fix. Refs #5044, #3419.
